# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 96 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 96 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_096_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 13

**1** I asked him, "Lord, show me also regarding the mountain with the most verdant grass, where the animals were feeding and the birds resting." **2** "All the nations that dwell under heaven," he said, "when they heard and believed were called by the name of the Son of God. **3** After receiving the seal they had one heart, one mind, one faith, one love. And they carried the spirits of the virgins with them. For this reason the tower appeared to be made of one stone." **4** "But what does the gate mean?" I asked. **5** "Listen," he said. "All these stones that went into the tower had to be brought in through the gate, and the gate is the Son of God; **6** this is the only entrance into the Lord, and no one else shall enter into him except through his Son. **7** Do you see this gate? How old is it — and yet how new! The grace given through the gate is new and fresh, and those who enter through it are the blessed, those who believe and live." **8** "Why then is the gate both old and new?" I asked. **9** "Listen," he said. "The Son of God is older than all creation, so that he was present as a counselor at the creation. **10** Therefore he is old. But the gate appeared new in the last days so that those who are about to be saved might enter through it into the kingdom of God. **11** Did you see," he said, "that the stones that came through the gate went into the building of the tower, but those which did not come through it were returned to their place?" **12** "I see, Lord," I said. "In this way also," he said, "no one shall enter the kingdom of God unless he takes the name of the Son of God. **13** For if you wish to enter into some city, and that city is surrounded by a wall and has only one gate, can you enter that city except through the gate which it has? **14** Therefore no one enters the kingdom of God except through the name of his Son, who is loved by him. Did you see the multitude of those who built the tower?" "I saw them, Lord," I said.

---

*EMET: the gate as the only entry — both old and new — is the fullest christological statement in the Shepherd. "Counselor at creation" (parabouleuomenos) is a striking term for pre-cosmic wisdom.*
